subject: MSA + Order Form: coverage rebalance and term alignment for renewal
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@acme.com>, Acme Corp Legal <legal@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form: coverage rebalance and term alignment for renewal

Elena / Acme legal team,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Attached is our proposed redline (MSA_Redline_initial.docx) that reflects the renewal items we discussed:

- Term: 24-month extension with a step-down option at month 12 for coverage reallocation.
- Capacity: 30% uplift across the Dedicated pool, reflected in OrderForm_v2.xlsx.
- SLAs: clarified SLO measurement windows and introduced a maximum credit cap (6% monthly).
- Indemnity & IP: scaled back mutual carveouts — we suggested limited third-party IP indemnity tied to proven claims.
- Data residency / audit access: committed to quarterly audit logs plus an on-site/secure-portal evidence option.

A couple of asks to accelerate:
1) Please flag any absolute no-go items for your counsel so we can isolate them before legal tradeoffs.
2) If you need a separate SOW for the capacity uplift (preferred by our Ops), call it out and we can draft.

Attached: MSA_Redline_initial.docx, OrderForm_v2.xlsx

Best,
David Kim
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Office: +1-415-555-0169
From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@acme.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Acme Corp Legal <legal@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: coverage rebalance and term alignment for renewal

David —

Thanks for the draft. We reviewed with internal counsel and have a set of redlines and comments (attached ACME_redlines_0701.docx). High level reaction:

- We cannot accept the proposed indemnity carveback as drafted; Acme needs broader IP protection for integrations our teams maintain.
- The SLA credit cap at 6% is acceptable only if measurement windows are aligned to calendar month close — otherwise we want a higher cap for persistent incidents.
- Data residency language is OK but we want KMS key management to be explicitly called out (customer-managed preferred).
- We prefer the uplift to sit on an amendment (addendum) rather than a standalone SOW; this helps our procurement.

We also flagged several small clarifications in the Order Form around billing cadence and overage calculation.

Attached: ACME_redlines_0701.docx

Can you get back to us with a response matrix and a revised redline by early next week? We are targeting signature the week of Jul 12.

Regards,
Elena Morris
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Acme Corp
elena.morris@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: ACME redlines — suggested positions and next steps

Forwarding ACME's comments. Quick internal read:

- Indemnity: Acme is asking for a materially broader IP indemnity. Markus, can legal propose a middle-ground that ties indemnity to (a) customer-provided integration code and (b) proven third-party claim? We should avoid an open-ended carveout.
- SLA cap: Ops/CS (Logan) — how feasible is 8% cap if we tighten the SLO windows to calendar month? Any telemetry limitations?
- KMS: Product (Kimberly), can we support explicit customer-managed KMS in Private deployments? If so, we should accept that language for Private but push a reasonable alternative for Hosted.
- Procurement preference for addendum vs SOW — low friction to convert the uplift into an Exhibit on the MSA; suggest we do Exhibit G (Capacity Addendum).

Proposed owner list:
- Legal (Markus): draft tracked redline + response matrix
- Product (Kimberly): confirm KMS feasibility and draft language
- CS/Ops (Logan): confirm SLA cap/monitoring implications
- AE (David/Marissa): lead commercial concessions and sign-off path

Related: HubSpot deal 78932 has the negotiated commercial terms noted — link below. I'm happy to jump on a 30-min call with ACME next week to close open points.

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/offer/78932, https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cMSA-redlines

-Marissa

Date: Sat, 03 Jul 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: coverage rebalance and term alignment for renewal

Elena — thanks for the quick turnaround and clear notes. Attached is Redwood's consolidated response and updated redline (MSA_Redline_2027-07-03.docx) plus a cleaned OrderForm_v3.xlsx reflecting the capacity uplift as an Exhibit. High-level positions: 

- Indemnity: we cannot accept an open-ended IP indemnity tied to customer integrations. Proposed compromise: broaden customer indemnity language to cover third-party IP claims where Acme can demonstrate that the claim arises from Redwood's delivered model or service (not customer code). We will accept targeted language for integrations where Redwood performed the integration work.
- SLA credit cap: we'll move to an 8% monthly cap on persistent incidents if we align measurement to calendar-month windows and include a three-strike escalation process.
- KMS: Kimberly confirmed customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; for Hosted we'll offer a written operational commitment and optional Bring-Your-Key pilot for an initial term.
- Amendment vs Exhibit: we propose Exhibit G (Capacity Addendum) attached to the MSA — keeps procurement happy and preserves single-signature flow.

Next steps requested:
1) Elena — please confirm whether the indemnity compromise above is workable for your counsel.
2) If yes, we will finalize redline and push DocuSign links the week of Jul 12.
3) If no, can you provide suggested language to narrow the disagreement?

Attachments: MSA_Redline_2027-07-03.docx (tracked), OrderForm_v3.xlsx

Appreciate the collaboration — happy to hop on a call Mon/Tue to knock this out.

Best regards,
David Kim
